content.rendered:
Our Mission:

To establish a dynamic and forward-looking alumni network for the Department of Civil Engineering at BAUST, Saidpur—one that fosters social, cultural, academic, and professional engagement among graduates. Our mission is to strengthen the bonds of unity and fellowship among alumni, while also supporting the continuous development of our department into a leading center of excellence in civil and infrastructure engineering. Through collaboration and contribution, we aim to play an active role in national development and in achieving the department’s vision. Our commitment is to remain connected with our alma mater and create meaningful opportunities for both current students and alumni.

Our Activities:

We aim to fulfill our mission through the following activities:

• Organizing seminars, technical workshops, and training sessions on current trends in civil engineering
• Coordinating educational field trips and industrial visits
• Hosting job fairs and recruitment events for fresh graduates
• Arranging social events such as reunions, departmental picnics, and annual dinners
• Supporting academic research and innovation projects
• Providing career counseling and mentoring programs
• Conducting quiz contests, technical competitions, and project showcases
• Facilitating cultural activities (in coordination with relevant clubs)
• Organizing blood donation drives and other community service programs
• Engaging in new initiatives proposed and approved by the executive committee

Alumni Association Committee:

The Civil Engineering Alumni Association was officially formed and it continues to grow with the active participation and support of our proud graduates.

content.rendered:
The Department of Civil Engineering at Bangladesh Army University of Science and Technology (BAUST), Saidpur, takes great pride in the achievements of its alumni. Our graduates have gone on to build successful careers in diverse fields, including government and private sector engineering roles, consultancy, construction, research, and higher education both at home and abroad.

This page serves as a testament to their accomplishments, showcasing where our alumni are making an impact—whether through professional contributions, advanced studies, or entrepreneurial ventures. It not only reflects the strength of our academic foundation but also inspires current and prospective students by highlighting the global footprint of our Civil Engineering graduates.

We invite you to explore the journeys of our alumni and celebrate the shared legacy of excellence that continues to grow with every graduating batch.

About ESC

ESC is a pioneer club of the Department of Civil Engineering.
It started the journey on 2nd September 2023 with the direct oversight and guidance of the
Head of the Department, Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, an Environmental Expert.

 

Aims

ESC aims to provide a platform for
individuals passionate about environmental sustainability to come together,
share ideas, and work towards a common goal of preserving and
protecting the planet for future generations.

Club Motto

Towards the sustainable environment: our earth our responsibility

 

Club Activities
  • Organize Workshops and Seminars on current environmental issues
  • Field Trips and Site Visits
  • Environmental Awareness Campaigns
  • Tree Planting Campaigns
  • Community Clean-Up Initiatives
  • Sustainable Infrastructure Projects exhibition
  • Research and Innovation
  • Community Engagement in Different Environmental Issues
  • Guest Speaker Series
  • Recycling and Waste Reduction Initiatives

The open channel flow laboratory is a specialized facility in civil engineering education focused on studying the behavior of water and other fluids in channels without full enclosure, such as rivers, canals, and spillways. It provides practical insights into fluid flow dynamics critical for water resources and hydraulic engineering.

 

Key Features of an Open Channel Flow Laboratory

Understanding uniform and non-uniform flow:
• Measuring velocity distribution, flow rates, and energy losses.
• Observing critical, subcritical, and supercritical flows.
• Relevance to Civil Engineering:

Hydraulic Structures: Designing efficient canals, culverts, and spillways.
Flood Management: Analyzing flow behavior for flood risk assessment.
Irrigation Engineering: Improving channel designs for optimal water distribution.

Learning Outcomes:
• Validate theoretical principles such as Manning’s equation and specific energy concepts.
• Gain skills in flow visualization and measurements.
• Understand environmental impacts and flow-related challenges.

A mechanical workshop is an essential part of engineering education, even for civil engineering students, as it equips them with hands-on skills in basic tools, machinery, and fabrication processes. Key Features of a Mechanical Workshop:
• Introduction to Tools and Equipment: Hand tools (Hammers, screwdrivers, spanners, and chisels etc.), Power tools (Drilling machines, grinders, and welding machines), Measuring instruments (Vernier calipers, micrometers, and gauges)
• Fabrication Processes: Welding, Cutting and Shaping, Fitting,

• Structural Fabrication: Learning the basics of steel structure assembly.
• Material Preparation: Practical exposure to handling materials like wood, metal, and concrete.
• Machine Maintenance: Understanding the upkeep of construction machinery.
• Practical Exposure: Students gain skills in crafting and repairing components. It enhances problem-solving abilities and fosters a safety-first approach during operations.

Surveying is vital for informed planning, construction, and management of land and infrastructure. It provides precise measurements of land boundaries, elevations, and contours, essential for designing buildings, roads, and utilities. In real estate, surveying defines property boundaries, preventing disputes and ensuring legal land ownership. For agriculture, it aids in irrigation planning and optimizing land use, supporting sustainable practices.

Surveying is also crucial for environmental conservation, helping assess habitat changes, track deforestation, and monitor climate impacts like rising sea levels. It plays a key role in mapping and navigation, forming the basis of GPS technology and supporting efficient logistics. In disaster management, surveying identifies flood zones and fault lines, enabling risk assessment and response planning.

The Structural Mechanics Laboratory plays a crucial role in civil engineering education by providing students with practical experience in understanding the behavior of structures under various loads. Through a series of hands-on experiments, students explore fundamental principles such as stress, strain, and deflection in materials and structural components. Ultimately, they prepare students for challenges in the field, ensuring they are equipped with the skills necessary to design safe and efficient structures in their future engineering careers.

4. Impact Test of Mild Steel Specimen

6. Compression Test of Helical Spring
7. Static Bending Test of Timber Beam
8. Buckling Test of Slender Column
9. Basics of Shear Force and Bending Moment

Common engineering materials in civil engineering include concrete, steel, wood, bricks, and asphalt, each serving unique roles in construction due to their distinct properties. Each material is chosen based on the structural needs, environmental conditions, and design requirements of the project, contributing to safe and efficient construction in civil engineering. Modern engineering also sees the use of advanced materials like carbon fiber and nanomaterials, which offer remarkable strength-to-weight ratios and enhanced properties, opening new possibilities in fields of Civil Engineering.

The Engineering Materials Lab in the Department of Civil Engineering at BAUST offers students valuable hands-on experience in testing various materials, including brick, stone aggregates, sand, cement, concrete, and soil. With a wide array of equipment available, the lab enables students to conduct undergraduate thesis work and pursue research projects under the guidance of experienced faculty within the department.

 

Performed Tests:

1. Determination of Normal Consistency of Cement with Vicat’s Apparatus
2. Determination of Initial Setting Time of Cement with Vicat’s Apparatus
3. Test for Direct Compressive Strength of Cement Mortar
4. Sieve Analysis of Fine and Coarse Aggregate
5. Specific Gravity (Relative Density) and Absorption Capacity of Fine Aggregate
6. Specific Gravity and Absorption Capacity of Coarse Aggregate
7. Unit Weight and Voids in Aggregate
8. Resistance to Degradation of Small Size Coarse Aggregate by Abrasion and Impact of the Los Angeles Machine
9. Determination of Slump, Air Content of Concrete and Compressive Strength of Cylindrical Concrete Specimens
10. Determination of Splitting Tensile Strength of Cylindrical Concrete Specimens
11. Sampling and Testing of Brick for Efflorescence, Compressive Strength and Absorption

Civil engineering drawing is a critical aspect of the design and construction process, providing a visual blueprint that guides every phase of a project. These drawings serve as detailed representations of infrastructure projects like roads, bridges, buildings, and water systems, translating complex design ideas into standardized formats that contractors, engineers, and builders can follow.

In today’s technology-driven world, computer-aided design software like AutoCAD, Revit, and ArchiCAD have revolutionized traditional hand-drawn plans, turning them into accurate, editable digital models. These tools enable efficient revisions, 3D visualization, and smooth collaboration across multidisciplinary teams, greatly enhancing the planning and execution of civil engineering projects.

However, hand-drawing enables students to unlock into their creativity and imagination, enhancing their skills in solving architectural challenges and developing more effective solutions for structural design. The expert faculties in the Department of Civil Engineering at BAUST upholds high standards to foster creativity and innovative thinking, preparing students to become the next generation of engineers for the nation.

 

Subjects Covered in the Civil Engineering Drawing Lab at BAUST

1. History and importance of Civil Engineering Drawing ,Drawing accessories and their uses
2. Line drawing
3. Lettering and Numbering: Drawing of standard letters and numbers
4. Drawing of linear geometric figures: pentagon, hexagon, octagon
5. Drawing of curved geometric figures: ellipse, parabola, hyperbola. First and third angle projections
6. Concept of isometric view, oblique view, theory of projections
7. Drawing of isometric view of 3D objects such as cube, prism, pyramid, cone and cylinder
8. Section of cubes, pyramids, cones, prisms, etc
9. Concept on Plan, elevation and section of single storied building
10. Drawing of Plan and elevation of single storied and a multistoried building

Overview

Civil engineering is the backbone of modern civilization—one of the oldest and most far-reaching disciplines in engineering. Civil engineers are the architects of infrastructure, shaping the physical world while ensuring environmental sustainability. From towering skyscrapers to sprawling dams, from cutting-edge suspension bridges to offshore drilling platforms, and from flood management to environmental protection, civil engineers make it all possible. They tackle challenges like earthquake resistance, pollution control, and sustainable development, all while managing projects and ensuring quality. In essence, civil engineers shape the history of nations and design a future built to last.

Civil Engineering at BAUST

The Department of Civil Engineering (CE) at BAUST embarked on its mission in December 2019, with the goal of producing top-tier civil engineers. Offering a comprehensive four-year B.Sc. degree in Civil Engineering, the department embraces a clear vision backed by strategic missions. Our Outcome-Based Education (OBE) system and cutting-edge curriculum cover the full spectrum of civil engineering fields, empowering students to specialize in areas that align with their career goals. Students first build a strong foundation in basic sciences, mathematics, humanities, social sciences, and management before diving into core civil engineering subjects. Specializations offered include Structural Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Transportation Engineering, and Water Resources Engineering.

Vision

To become a recognized center of excellence through producing Civil Engineering professionals inculcating morality, ethics, and discipline, and fitted for industry and academia to ensure sustainable development.

Mission

Below specified missions are followed by the department to grasp the vision:

  • To ensure a dynamic, student-centered learning environment with state-of-the-art facilities in Civil Engineering, including basic sciences and management.
  • To provide opportunities that bridge theoretical knowledge with real-time projects and industrial activities, contributing to the sustainable development of society.
  • To conduct advanced, inter- and multi-disciplinary research in collaboration with industries and other academia to address contemporary challenges.
  • To foster students’ engagement in lifelong learning, cultivating appreciation for diversity, tolerance, ethics, and morality.

PEOs

  • Graduates will be competent to provide effective solutions to civil engineering problems by applying appropriate knowledge, skills, and tools.
  • Graduates will responsibly practice civil engineering by integrating sustainability, safety, economic feasibility, and ethical values to meet societal needs.
  • Graduates will demonstrate communication, leadership, teamwork, and project management skills in multidisciplinary and diverse professional environments.
  • Graduates will engage in lifelong learning through higher studies, professional training, research, or entrepreneurship to address emerging technologies and evolving challenges for professional advancement.

Why Choose CE at BAUST?

The main features of CE at BAUST are:

  • Outcome Based Education (OBE) system
  • Updated curricula and syllabi
  • Highly qualified faculty members and staffs
  • Students-centered class environment
  • State-of-the art laboratories
  • Continuous monitoring of the students
  • Extra- and Co-curricular activities
  • Collaboration with industries and universities
  • Merit scholarships
  • 100% hall facilities (male and female)
  • Waiver for freedom fighter’s children, siblings and wards of military personnel
